error.text:
{
  "critical": [
    {
      "file": ".github/workflows/review.yml",
      "startLine": 86,
      "endLine": 87,
      "issue": "Potential command injection via PR body override",
      "details": "The sed regex for extracting the Plan: override from PR_BODY allows any characters in the path except whitespace and control characters. While it anchors at both ends and restricts to context/(changes|archive)/, the character class `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]` still allows `../` path traversal segments. Although a later check rejects `*..*`, this only catches literal `..` and not encoded variants or other traversal techniques. The PR body is attacker-controlled, so this could allow reading unintended files if the check is bypassed.",
      "remediation": "Replace the traversal check with a more robust validation that normalizes the path (e.g., using `realpath` or a path library) and ensures it stays within the expected directories. Consider using a stricter character class that disallows `.` entirely except for the `.md` extension."
    },
    {
      "file": ".github/workflows/review.yml",
      "startLine": 126,
      "endLine": 127,
      "issue": "Symlink attack via plan staging",
      "details": "The plan staging step uses `git show` to read the blob, which correctly prevents symlink following. However, the mode check only accepts `100644` and `100755`. If a PR creates a plan file as a symlink (mode 120000), the step will reject it. But if the symlink points to a sensitive file and the mode check were to be weakened or removed in the future, this could lead to reading sensitive files (like /proc/self/environ) and exposing them in the AI review prompt.",
      "remediation": "The current protection is adequate, but add a comment explaining why symlinks are rejected and documenting the security implications. Consider adding explicit logging when a symlink is detected to aid in debugging potential attacks."
    }
  ],
  "major": [
    {
      "file": ".github/workflows/review.yml",
      "startLine": 143,
      "endLine": 146,
      "issue": "Empty diff handling may skip important reviews",
      "details": "When the diff becomes empty after excluding reviews/** and the plan file, the entire AI review is skipped. This means a PR that only modifies excluded files (like moving a plan to archive) receives no code review at all, potentially missing important changes in other files that weren't excluded.",
      "remediation": "Instead of skipping the entire review, consider running the review on the non-excluded files only. If the diff is truly empty after exclusions, post a comment explaining why no review was performed rather than silently skipping."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/cli.ts",
      "startLine": 215,
      "endLine": 226,
      "issue": "Plan path logging may expose sensitive information",
      "details": "The plan path from PLAN_PATH env var is logged to stderr. While control characters are defused, the actual path could contain sensitive information if the PR body references unexpected paths. This log appears in GitHub Actions logs which may be publicly visible.",
      "remediation": "Sanitize the logged path more aggressively, e.g., only showing the last two path components, or completely omit the path from logs and only log the character count."
    }
  ],
  "minor": [
    {
      "file": ".github/actions/ai-review/action.yml",
      "startLine": 13,
      "endLine": 16,
      "issue": "Inconsistent description of review passes",
      "details": "The description mentions 'Two-pass AI review' but the implementation actually has three passes when a plan is present. This could confuse users reading the action metadata.",
      "remediation": "Update the description to accurately reflect the three-pass nature: 'Two-pass AI review (finder + judge) over the PR diff, plus optional third pass when a plan is resolved'."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/config.ts",
      "startLine": 25,
      "endLine": 33,
      "issue": "Duplicate model configuration",
      "details": "DEFAULT_IMPL_REVIEW_MODEL is set to the same value as DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL (claude-sonnet-5). While they're separate constants for tunability, using the same default model could lead to confusion and unnecessary costs if both passes run with the same expensive model.",
      "remediation": "Consider using a cheaper model (like claude-haiku) as the default for implementation review, or add a comment explaining why the same model is intentionally used."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/cli.ts",
      "startLine": 62,
      "endLine": 66,
      "issue": "Error message doesn't include new --plan-file option",
      "details": "The usage string in the error for unknown arguments doesn't include the new --plan-file option, which could confuse users trying to use the feature.",
      "remediation": "Update the usage string to include all available options: '--diff-file <path> [--out-dir <dir>] [--project-context-file <path>] [--source-root <dir>] [--plan-file <path>]'"
    }
  ],
  "nit": [
    {
      "file": ".github/workflows/review.yml",
      "startLine": 95,
      "endLine": 95,
      "issue": "Inconsistent quoting in array expansion",
      "details": "The EXCLUDES array uses double quotes for the first element but no quotes for the conditional second element. While functionally correct, inconsistent quoting style can reduce readability.",
      "remediation": "Use consistent quoting: `EXCLUDES=(':(exclude,glob)**/reviews/*.md')` and `EXCLUDES+=(\":(exclude)${PLAN_PATH}\")`"
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/cli.test.ts",
      "startLine": 447,
      "endLine": 447,
      "issue": "Test comment references wrong PR number",
      "details": "The comment mentions 'PR #127, run 31703938953' but this is just an example reference that may become outdated and confusing.",
      "remediation": "Replace with a generic description like 'a recent production run' or remove the specific reference."
    }
  ],
  "testing": [
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/cli.test.ts",
      "startLine": 428,
      "endLine": 428,
      "issue": "Missing test for plan file size limit",
      "details": "The implementation caps plan files at 40KB (mentioned in plan-brief.md) but there's no test verifying this limit is enforced. Large plan files could exceed model context limits.",
      "remediation": "Add a test that verifies plan files larger than 40KB are truncated and that planTruncated is set in the result."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/impl-reviewer.test.ts",
      "startLine": 1,
      "endLine": 1,
      "issue": "New implementation reviewer lacks comprehensive tests",
      "details": "The impl-reviewer.test.ts file exists but the diff was truncated. Given the complexity of the implementation review logic (seven dimensions, verdict grading), it likely needs more test coverage for edge cases and failure modes.",
      "remediation": "Ensure full test coverage for: empty plans, malformed plans, plans without exclusions, all seven dimensions individually, and error handling."
    }
  ],
  "documentation": [
    {
      "file": "AGENTS.md",
      "startLine": 94,
      "endLine": 102,
      "issue": "Documentation doesn't explain the empty diff skip behavior",
      "details": "The documentation mentions the new third pass but doesn't explain that PRs with only plan/review document changes are skipped entirely. This could confuse users when their PR receives no review.",
      "remediation": "Add a note explaining: 'PRs that only contain plan files or review documents are excluded from review to avoid noise. Such PRs will show a skip notice in the check run.'"
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/code-reviewer/src/config.ts",
      "startLine": 25,
      "endLine": 33,
      "issue": "Model choice rationale not documented",
      "details": "The comment explains why sonnet-5 was chosen but doesn't document the trade-offs or alternatives. Future maintainers may not understand the cost/benefit analysis.",
      "remediation": "Expand the comment to include: estimated cost per review, why haiku wasn't sufficient, and what would trigger reconsidering the model choice."
    }
  ]
}
